skill.name: aws-compliance-checker
skill.description: Checks AWS environments against CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2 controls with AWS CLI and boto3 examples.
skill.summary: Run AWS compliance checks and generate audit reports for common security frameworks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill contains many Markdown examples for AWS compliance checks. Most static hits are formatting artifacts or expected compliance literals, but several AWS CLI substitutions are confirmed because they enumerate cloud configuration with user credentials.

remediation.issue: AWS CLI examples can enumerate sensitive account metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before execution and document the minimum read-only IAM permissions for each check.

remediation.issue: Command output may include user names, bucket names, access key IDs, and resource identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction guidance and prefer summarized output for shared reports.

remediation.issue: Example scripts omit execution guardrails and dependency checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add profile, region, dependency, and error-handling guidance before users run the examples in production.

content.value_statement: AWS teams need repeatable checks for common audit controls. This skill provides CLI and boto3 checks for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2.
actual_capabilities: Provides CIS AWS Foundations checks for IAM, logging, monitoring, and network controls.
Includes AWS CLI examples for CloudTrail, AWS Config, S3 logging, VPC flow logs, and security groups.
Includes boto3 examples for PCI-DSS checks across EC2, RDS, S3, IAM, and CloudTrail.
Generates a basic compliance report structure with pass, fail, and score fields.
Lists prompts and practices for recurring AWS compliance reviews.
limitations: It is a template and does not replace formal audit evidence or legal compliance review.
Several Python report functions are placeholders and need implementation before production use.
It depends on AWS credentials, permissions, AWS CLI, jq, and boto3 in the user environment.
It reports selected control checks and may not cover every framework requirement.

use_cases.title: Run CIS Baseline Checks
use_cases.description: Review IAM, logging, monitoring, and network controls before a scheduled security review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Audit Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect structured findings for PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or SOC 2 readiness discussions.

use_cases.title: Find Cloud Control Gaps
use_cases.description: Identify missing logging, weak encryption, and public ingress before remediation planning.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic CIS Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of common AWS security controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to review IAM, CloudTrail, AWS Config, and security group settings for my AWS account. Ask before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Review PCI-DSS Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to assess PCI-DSS readiness for my AWS environment. Summarize network, encryption, MFA, and logging gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Audit Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evidence collection for compliance teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to create an AWS compliance report for CIS and HIPAA. Include findings, severity, affected services, and remediation owners.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Continuous Monitoring
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operating model for recurring audits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to design a recurring AWS compliance workflow. Include permissions, schedule, redaction rules, evidence retention, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Check CIS IAM controls for a production account.
output: Users without MFA listed for review.
Old access keys identified with age information.

output_examples.input: Prepare HIPAA audit notes for AWS controls.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes access control, audit logging, encryption at rest, and transmission security checks with recommended remediation steps.

best_practices: Use read-only AWS credentials with least privilege before running checks.
Redact account identifiers, user names, bucket names, and access key IDs in shared reports.
Validate results with AWS Security Hub, AWS Config, and a qualified auditor.
anti_patterns: Run checks with administrator credentials when read-only permissions are enough.
Treat generated findings as final compliance attestation without review.
Share raw command output in tickets or chat without redaction.

faq.question: Does this skill change AWS resources?
faq.answer: The documented checks are read-oriented. Users should still review every command before execution.

faq.question: Which compliance frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: It covers examples for CIS AWS Foundations, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The examples rely on AWS CLI, jq, Python, boto3, and valid AWS credentials.

faq.question: Can it produce formal audit evidence?
faq.answer: It can support evidence collection, but a qualified auditor must validate final evidence.

faq.question: Does it support multiple AWS accounts?
faq.answer: The examples can be adapted for profiles or account loops, but this is not fully automated.

faq.question: How should results be shared?
faq.answer: Share summarized findings and redact identifiers before sending reports outside the security team.
